title: Mammoth Lakes, California
seoTitle: Charter Bus to Mammoth Lakes, California: Group Guide
excerpt: A charter bus to Mammoth Lakes handles the long Sierra drive and the snow. Which vehicle fits, when the roads close, and what a group can do year-round.

heroImage.alt: Alpine lakes and granite peaks of the Mammoth Lakes Basin in the eastern Sierra Nevada

extraImage.alt: A skier boarding a coach at the base of Mammoth Mountain on a winter morning

body.text: Mammoth Lakes sits at nearly 8,000 feet on the eastern side of the Sierra Nevada, which gives it two things few mountain towns have: a genuinely long snow season and a summer that is all alpine lakes and granite. It is also a long way from anywhere. That combination is why a charter bus to Mammoth Lakes makes more sense than driving — the approach is five hours of mountain highway, and on a ski weekend it can be five hours in chains.
A winter town and a summer town

In winter Mammoth Mountain runs one of the longest seasons in North America, frequently from November into May and occasionally beyond. Groups come for the skiing, and the town is built to absorb them — the shuttle system between lodging, the village and the lifts is genuinely good, which means the coach can park and stay parked once you arrive.

In summer the same town becomes a base for the Mammoth Lakes Basin, Minaret Vista, and Devils Postpile National Monument, where columnar basalt rises sixty feet in near-perfect hexagons and Rainbow Falls drops a hundred feet a short walk further on.
Devils Postpile and the mandatory shuttle

This one catches groups out. In summer, access to Devils Postpile and Reds Meadow is restricted during the day and visitors are required to use a mandatory shuttle from the Mammoth Mountain Adventure Center rather than driving the road themselves. Your charter bus takes the group to the shuttle, not to the monument. Build that transfer into the schedule — it is straightforward once you know, and an unpleasant surprise if you do not.
Which charter bus suits a Mammoth trip

items: Forty to fifty-six: a full-size [charter bus](/fleet/motor-coaches) is the right vehicle for the long haul from Southern California, with luggage bays that take skis and boards without anyone holding them.
Twenty to thirty-two: a [mini bus](/fleet/mini-buses) handles the town's tighter lodging entrances and is easier on winter roads.
Ten to fourteen: a [sprinter van](/fleet/sprinter-vans) suits a small ski group or a family party.
Team travel: our [sports team travel](/services/sports-team-travel) bookings run heavily into Mammoth through the racing season, and equipment space is usually the deciding factor.

body.text: Getting there, and the roads that close

US-395 is the only practical approach, and it stays open year-round. Tioga Pass, the direct route from Yosemite, does not — it closes with the first heavy snow and often does not reopen until late May or June, which adds several hours to any trip routed that way in winter or spring. Check the pass status before finalizing a route rather than trusting a mapping app.

From Los Angeles it is about five hours, from [Reno](/locations/nevada/reno) around three, and from [Bishop](/locations/california/bishop) forty minutes. Groups searching for charter bus rental near me for a Sierra ski trip should confirm the operator runs winter-equipped vehicles and drivers experienced with chain controls — on US-395 in January that is the difference between arriving and not.

The town sits at 7,880 feet and the mountain tops out above 11,000. Groups arriving from sea level frequently feel it on the first day: shortness of breath, headaches, poor sleep. Plan a gentle first afternoon rather than a hard one, and tell the group to drink far more water than usual. It is the most common complaint on a Mammoth trip and almost entirely preventable.
What the group does when it is not skiing

Not everyone on a ski trip skis, and Mammoth handles that better than most mountain towns. The Village at Mammoth is compact and walkable with restaurants and shops, the gondola runs to the 11,053-foot summit for anyone who wants the view without the descent, and the hot springs scattered across the Long Valley Caldera east of town are a genuinely memorable afternoon.

In summer the range widens considerably. The lakes basin has flat, easy walking around Twin Lakes and Lake Mary, Hot Creek Geological Site is fifteen minutes from town, and Bodie, a preserved gold-rush ghost town, sits about ninety minutes north — a strong half-day for a group that wants something other than a trail.

Any of these can be built around the coach, which is the advantage of keeping the vehicle for the duration rather than booking transfers at each end. Skiers get dropped at the lifts, everybody else gets a different itinerary, and the group still has dinner together.

items: November to May: ski season, with the best conditions typically January through March. Book vehicles early for holiday weekends.
June to September: hiking, fishing and the lakes basin, with wildflowers at their best in July. Warm days and cold nights.
October and early November: quiet, cheap and often beautiful, but most summer services have closed and the snow has not yet arrived.
